content:
Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed (D-Mich.) revealed to Politico’s Playbook on Wednesday that he’s been “comparing notes” with New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani on how to work with Donald Trump in hopes of getting the president to support “Medicare for All” legislation.

“He understands, just like I understand, that even if you might disagree with the president on a whole host of issues, he’s the president of the United States,” El-Sayed said of Mamdani, who has developed an unusually friendly relationship with the president considering their political differences.

“I’ll work with anybody when it comes to try and get money out of politics, put money in pockets, and pass Medicare for All,” he added.

El-Sayed — who, like Mamdani, is a trailblazing Muslim politician as well as a progressive Democrat — has looked to court the president on Medicare for All by sharing images of a gold-colored “Trumpcare” card mock-up on his social media pages.

“This is a message for @realDonald Trump,” El-Sayed wrote in a post. “Donald, this is on the table. Guarantee healthcare for every American, from cradle to grave.”

Trump — who shared the images of the mock card with no further input to his Truth Social platform earlier this month — called El-Sayed a “smart guy” in an interview with the New York Post on Tuesday, adding that he’ll be meeting with the senator-elect on the proposal at a later unspecified date.

When asked if he thinks Trump, who fueled Islamophobic attacks against him in the lead-up to the midterms this year, is serious about a deal, El-Sayed told Politico’s Playbook, “Let’s see what comes up in the conversation.”

Back in July, Mamdani revealed to Rolling Stone magazine that his approach to working with the president stems from wanting to be “honest” with him, noting that “honesty is in places of disagreement.”
